packet.title: THE BIBLICAL WORLD V2 — VERIFIED SOURCE & ASSET PACKET
packet.note: This registry imports claims and licensing conclusions from the user-supplied verification packet. The current execution environment has no live web access, so entries are marked packet-verified rather than independently re-verified by this build.

resources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
resources.attribution: Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved.
resources.notes: Packet classifies cropping, Terrain-RGB conversion, PMTiles packaging, Cloudflare R2 hosting, GitHub Pages use, and derived-tile distribution as allowed. GLO-30 is a modern DSM, not ancient terrain.

resources.name: Natural Earth
resources.notes: Use for modern macro-geography only; not as an ancient coastline source.

resources.name: Pleiades: A Gazetteer of Past Places
resources.attribution: Pleiades: A Gazetteer of Past Places (https://pleiades.stoa.org), used under CC BY 4.0.
resources.notes: Use as a linked-data identifier and ancient-place reference. Coordinates remain secondary to the atlas evidence model for disputed sites.

resources.name: Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire (DARE) Roman roads
resources.attribution: Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire (DARE), Johan Åhlfeldt, Lund University, published under CC BY 4.0.
resources.notes: Packet supplies a roads.geojson download path and classifies PMTiles conversion as allowed. Exact road alignments should still be presented as archaeological/historical network data rather than exact routes taken by biblical individuals.

resources.name: AWMC Antiquity À-la-carte
resources.attribution: Ancient World Mapping Center (UNC Chapel Hill), published under CC BY 4.0.
resources.notes: Packet explicitly treats AWMC and DARE as independently licensed resources.

resources.name: Wikidata structured data
resources.attribution: No attribution required for structured data; project retains source links as good practice.
resources.notes: Use QIDs and external identifiers as cross-references. Do not use P625 as primary evidence for disputed ancient locations.

resources.name: ORBIS: The Stanford Geospatial Network Model of the Roman World
resources.attribution: ORBIS: The Stanford Geospatial Network Model of the Roman World, used under CC BY-NC 3.0.
resources.notes: Do not make ORBIS a required production dependency. Prefer DARE/AWMC for redistributable road geometry; ORBIS may remain a research/reference model unless commercial licensing is obtained.

resources.name: Open Context archaeological datasets
resources.attribution: Cite the specific dataset DOI, authors, and license.
resources.notes: Repository policy alone is not sufficient approval for an individual archaeological dataset. Verify each dataset record before ingestion.

resources.name: Library of Congress G. Eric and Edith Matson Photograph Collection
resources.attribution: Library of Congress, G. Eric and Edith Matson Photograph Collection.
resources.notes: Verify the individual LOC item record before binding a specific photograph. Historic imagery documents later landscapes, not ancient appearance.

resources.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access
resources.license: CC0 1.0 Universal for marked Open Access images
resources.attribution: Courtesy of The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access / CC0).
resources.notes: Verify that each selected object image is individually marked Open Access before local hosting.

resources.name: Digital Augustan Rome
resources.attribution: Digital Augustan Rome, used under CC BY-NC 4.0.
resources.notes: Keep optional and replace with an unrestricted source for any commercial release.

claims.statement: Eastern Nile Delta paleogeography may be reconstructed as a marsh/lake environment, but the packet does not support an exact Exodus crossing coordinate.
citations: Drews, C. & Han, W. (2010), PLOS ONE 5(8): e12481, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0012481
claims.guardrail: Never render a single crossing point or route as established.

claims.statement: The Drews & Han hydrodynamic model demonstrates a physical wind-setdown mechanism under modeled conditions; it does not demonstrate that the Exodus event occurred.
citations: Drews, C. & Han, W. (2010). Dynamics of Wind Setdown at Suez and the Eastern Nile Delta. PLOS ONE 5(8): e12481. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0012481
claims.guardrail: Present only as environmental/physical modeling, never as proof of the biblical event.

claims.statement: The verification packet preserves Mount Sinai as geographically unresolved and treats proposed locations as traditional/candidate hypotheses.
citations: User-supplied V2 verification packet, Sinai / Exodus Evidence Register
claims.guardrail: Do not create an established Mount Sinai coordinate or a single Exodus route.

claims.statement: The packet preserves the High Chronology versus Low Chronology debate for the attribution/dating of monumental Iron Age architecture at Megiddo.
citations: User-supplied V2 verification packet, Megiddo / Canaan Evidence Register
claims.guardrail: Do not label the six-chambered gate or palatial architecture as undeniably Solomonic.

claims.statement: The packet does not support an archaeologically established First Temple architectural footprint on the Temple Mount.
citations: User-supplied V2 verification packet, Jerusalem Evidence Register / Unresolved Register
claims.guardrail: Any First Temple model must remain textual/comparative/artistic reconstruction, not mapped excavation geometry.

claims.statement: The packet classifies Herod's western palace as the strongly favored model for Pilate's Jerusalem praetorium while retaining uncertainty about the exact judgment location.
claims.guardrail: Keep the western-palace model probable rather than established; retain the Antonia/Via Dolorosa tradition separately.

claims.statement: The packet supports the Church of the Holy Sepulchre area as the leading historical/archaeological candidate while rejecting absolute coordinate certainty.
claims.guardrail: Keep textual Golgotha and Jesus' tomb coordinate-free; map traditions/candidates separately.

claims.statement: The packet describes el-Araj as favored by its active excavators while et-Tell remains an active competing identification.
citations: Aviam, M. & Notley, R. S. (2018). Near Eastern Archaeology 81(4), 254-260
claims.guardrail: Keep both sites as candidates; do not promote one to established Bethsaida.

claims.statement: The Gospel mountain remains unnamed; Hermon may be presented as a geographical proposal and Tabor as traditional, neither as an established identification.
citations: User-supplied V2 verification packet, Caesarea Philippi / Transfiguration section
claims.guardrail: Do not pin the textual Transfiguration mountain.

claims.statement: The packet supports a substantially different Roman-period Ephesus coastline and an active marine harbor, while exact decade-specific shoreline geometry remains interpolated.
citations: Kraft, J. C., Brückner, H., Kayan, I. & Engelmann, H. (2007). The Paleogeography of Ancient Ephesus. Geoarchaeology 22(1), 121-149
claims.guardrail: Any historical shoreline polygon must be labeled reconstructed and period-specific.

claims.statement: Visionary entities such as New Jerusalem, Babylon the Great, and the Abyss remain coordinate-free and must not be placed on terrestrial DEM terrain.
citations: User-supplied V2 verification packet, Revelation / Roman Asia Register
claims.guardrail: Keep visionary geography in the separate non-spatial renderer.

sceneAssessments.note: Research packet marks evidence inputs ready; this repository does not yet bundle or host the DEM.
Exact paleolake geometry still needs independently authored vector reconstruction from cited research.
Repository has not ingested a specific licensed Megiddo dataset yet.
Ancient surface remains a reconstruction; Temple Mount subsurface and Third Wall remain unresolved.
The -209m claim is research-packet supplied; a production shoreline geometry is not yet present.
No Pedersén GIS source file is bundled in this repository.
Historical coastline must be independently reconstructed and labeled as such.
DARE is preferred for redistributable road geometry; ORBIS/Digital Augustan Rome remain optional non-commercial research layers.
